endpointObservation.interpretation: Provider accepted the HTTP request and sent model-labelled SSE deltas. No HTTP refusal or provider error frame is present in the retained stream; HTTP 200 does not establish a completed response.

partialStream.timingCaveat: SSE created fields are provider-supplied seconds, not recorded local arrival times. Keep-alives have no timestamps. Exact time to first byte/token and the split between provider queueing, prefill and inference cannot be recovered.
partialStream.accountingCaveat: Fragments, characters and SSE bytes are not tokens. No tokenizer or token-rate estimate was substituted for missing provider usage.

usageAndCost.interpretation: The zero sum covers zero completed responses. It is not a measured failed-call bill, zero token usage, zero resource consumption or independent billing evidence.

timing.caveat: Local file mtimes locate receipt writes, not instrumented timer firing or network arrival. The provider timer is created immediately after task/input and runtime-copy writes.

inMemoryRuntimeCheck.method: new AbortController(); abort(); inspect signal.reason only; zero I/O, timers, provider or model calls

abortAnalysis.bestSupportedCause: The adapter's own 150-second total-call deadline aborted an unfinished HTTP 200 stream and terminated its sandbox.
abortAnalysis.confidence: Strong inference from exact source, local timing, error identity and saved generator status; the original receipt lacks an explicit abort cause/time field.
abortAnalysis.sourceDefectEstablished: A fetch/body AbortError is wrapped as MODEL_TRANSPORT and stored in transportFailure. The final selector prefers transportFailure before checking deadlineExpired or caller signal. A deadline cancellation can therefore be mislabeled as transport failure; callback ordering can affect which label survives.
support: Adapter src/opencode-v2-free.mjs:203-208 writes inputs/copies, creates a shared controller, and starts the 150000ms timer before catalog/private-server startup.
Adapter :233-256 passes that controller to provider fetch, saves partial body bytes, wraps the resulting untyped abort as MODEL_TRANSPORT, and stores it via stop at :218.
Adapter :267-268 also passes that controller to runProcess and prefers transportFailure on subprocess rejection; :292-295 again prefers it before deadlineExpired.
Process helper src/process.mjs:20-27 sends SIGTERM on cancellation. The observed subprocess age149780ms is below its own150000ms timer, which starts later than the adapter timer.

Generator src/generator.mjs:119-124 marks an aborted generator controller cancelled. The saved job is failed, and its360000ms budget was not reached. This supports internal provider cancellation rather than propagated caller/outer-budget cancellation.
unsupportedAlternatives: No saved HTTP401/403/429/5xx or provider-error frame supports access refusal, rate limiting or an explicit remote failure.
No saved socket-reset, DNS, TLS, premature-EOF or network error cause supports a remote disconnect; original nested network cause metadata was not retained.
No4MiB response overflow occurred;199373 bytes were retained. There is no terminal length reason or measured token count proving the8192-token limit was reached.
abortAnalysis.remainingUncertainty: deadlineExpired, controller.signal.reason, caller-signal state and first-failure timing were not persisted. A coincident unrecorded event cannot be categorically excluded from these receipts alone.

missingReceiptInterpretation: The outer SIGTERM can terminate the sandbox driver before its awaited CLI result is saved and before native export/final logging. Its empty outer stdout/stderr are not evidence of an empty upstream stream. No native database was opened to infer success or usage.

nextDiscriminatingChange.firstStep: In a separately reviewed source revision, record the first terminal cause before aborting. Preserve TIMEOUT for an adapter deadline, CANCELLED for caller cancellation, and the original earlier transport/HTTP error when that error initiated shutdown. Keep the later AbortError as a secondary observation.
nextDiscriminatingChange.offlineDiscriminator: Use supplied HTTP200/SSE that remains open until a short deadline, caller cancellation before the deadline, a supplied network read error before the deadline, and429/403. Assert distinct primary causes, partial-byte retention, one forwarded attempt and no retry. A transport error that precedes the timer must not be overwritten by a later timeout.
nextDiscriminatingChange.laterExperimentOnlyWithSeparateAuthoriza: After cause-label tests and a fresh freeze, a single larger fixed wall-clock budget on the same public prompt/model/output cap can test whether additional time reaches final content and terminal usage. Preserve the150s run as censored evidence. Keep no fallback/retry and the exact completion/export gates. This would be a new budget condition, not a retroactive pass or matched-quality comparison.

claimBoundary: The frozen campaign did not complete within its150s provider-call window. The trace contains partial reasoning but no candidate, so it cannot establish workflow correctness, a model-quality negative, comparative model performance, or future completion under more time.
